{{Quote|&hellip; You are part of the greatest navy ever assembled. The might of the Empire rests on the military &mdash; and the Imperial Navy embodies the most elite and trusted segment of that power. Only the best, the most disciplined, are admitted to our ranks. We who serve the Emperor in the Imperial Navy have made this Empire the irresistible, galaxy-spanning force it is today.|Fleet Admiral Holt, cadet indoctrination speech excerpt|<ref name="ISB2">[[Imperial Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''Imperial Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref>}}
The '''Imperial Navy''', also known as the '''Imperial Starfleet''', '''Imperial Fleet''', '''Imperial Battlefleet''', '''Imperial Space Navy''', or '''Imperial Space Service''', and informally referred to as "'''the Empire's long arm''',"<ref name="ISB2" /> was the [[Space warfare/Legends|space warfare]] branch of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. At its peak, it fielded millions of [[Warship/Legends|warships]], logistics vessels and [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]], becoming one of the largest [[Navy/Legends|navies]] in galactic history and maintaining Imperial control throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].

The Imperial Navy was formed from the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], as part of the newly-proclaimed [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine's]] [[Imperialization/Legends|Imperialization]] campaign during the rise of the Empire.<ref name="DL:TRODV">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref> A reorganized command structure, eventually consisting of twelve [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]],<ref name="WW:IGA">{{InsiderCite|66|Who's Who: Imperial Grand Admirals}}</ref> supervised the rapid expansion of the fleet that had begun during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Growing discontent with the New Order eventually coalesced into the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], which began a military campaign against Imperial forces, that became known as the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] was charged by Emperor Palpatine with overseeing the Imperial Navy's efforts in stomping the insurrection and hunting the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Rebel fleet]].

After the loss of both Emperor Palpatine and [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader in the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], the Empire began to devolve into warlordism and infighting, splintering the Imperial Navy. Though the Navy would fight on under a succession of leaders, including [[Ysanne Isard]], [[Zsinj|Warlord Zsinj]], Grand Admiral [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], the reborn Emperor, and [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Natasi Daala|Daala]], it would not again become a cohesive unit until the Empire reconsolidated itself of the [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] under Grand Admiral [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]], becoming a veritable fighting force once again under his command during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. The Imperial Navy would regain much of its former strength by the time of the [[Fel Empire]], under which it fought the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] in the [[Sith–Imperial War]]. The Navy would be split into those [[Empire-in-exile|loyal]] to [[Roan Fel]] and those who served [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] in the subsequent [[Second Imperial Civil War|civil war]].<ref name="SWL0½">[[Star Wars: Legacy (2006) 0½|''Star Wars: Legacy'' (2006) 0½]]</ref>

The Imperial Navy was one of the most formidable militaries ever assembled, consisting of millions of warships, fighters and transports, manned by trillions of fleet crew.<ref name="RECG">''[[Rebellion Era Campaign Guide]]''</ref> The mainstays of its fleets&mdash;the [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] and [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] capital ships<ref name="DESB">''[[Dark Empire Sourcebook]]''</ref> and the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighter]] series of starfighters&mdash;became some of the most visible symbols of Imperial rule to the galaxy's civilian populace.<ref name="ISB">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref>

==Role==
{{Quote|The Empire, on the other hand, maintains massive fleets containing up to two dozen capital ships&mdash;few would dare to challenge such a formidable force. These vessels boast heavy armor plating, high-powered shielding, and an enormous amount of firepower, making them capable of reducing an entire planet to nothing more than charred remains. Truly these are the most awesome weapons of war ever constructed&hellip;|[[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Elpfel]], commanding officer of the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]] ''[[Wavesong]]''|<ref name="Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition">''[[Star Wars Trilogy Sourcebook, Special Edition]]''</ref>}}
[[File:TIE-D_IVEP.png|thumb|left|250px|An Imperial fleet in planetary orbit]]
The role of the Imperial Navy was the absolute dominance of known space in the name of the Empire,<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref> as well as enforcing the Emperor's will.<ref name="Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref><ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Conan Antonio Motti/Legends|Conan Antonio Motti]] identified four key functions of the Imperial Navy, including [[Blockade/Legends|blockading]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceports]] to cripple a [[Planet/Legends|planet's]] ability to fight, [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|bombarding]] planets to destroy enemy infrastructure, guarding shipping lanes against [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] and [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] to safeguard commerce and frighten criminals into conducing honest trade, and transporting and supporting other branches of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] from space and from the air, supplying them with space and aerial support upon disembarkation if necessary.<ref name="Handbook" /> In large part because of the requirement of traveling throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] in the Navy, a tour of duty for naval officers often resulted in them encountering various unique peoples and visiting various exotic worlds.<ref name="TRG1">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]</ref>

In addition, the Imperial Navy was charged with freeing the system space of member worlds from hazards to profitable commerce, assuring the safety of member worlds from attack from outside forces, and bolstering the planetary governments in times of crisis, which was one of the few instances where the Navy was unchanged in role from that of the Old Republic. However, a major difference was that, regarding the bolstering of planetary governments during crises, the Imperial Navy under the New Order could do so pre-emptively without waiting for a majority vote in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Senate]], while the Republic Navy needed to wait at least seven days for conflicts to resolve before, upon getting a majority vote, interfering. Since the [[Dissolution of the Imperial Senate/Legends|Dissolution of the Imperial Senate]], the Navy, largely due to no longer being required to wait for a vote from the Senate, often got civilian orders transmitted at the level of the Sector Group, with the orders coming from regional Moffs, Grand Moffs, or even the Emperor, and likewise smaller units only were to receive orders from officers in the proper chain of command. This was a change from the Republic Navy: originally, senators or other politically powerful beings could directly commandeer naval vessels&mdash;or in some cases entire squadrons&mdash;without the order needing to come down through the chain of command. In addition, the Imperial Navy was required to work alongside the Imperial Army in a support role during critical phases of various military operations and even to some extent [[Ground support wing|supply some of its assets]] to permanent Army outposts. This was a contrast to the Republic Navy, which generally was the military branch pre&ndash;Clone Wars that was paid for by the Republic as a whole and was stretched too thin to play any role in the barely existent Republic Army during combat operations and at best ferried them between destinations, with the Republic Navy's expenditures remaining stable while the Republic Army's expenditures decreasing due to complaints by nonwealthy member worlds due to excessive costs at maintaining them.<ref name="ISB2" />

The Imperial Navy's doctrine was heavily influenced by the experience of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], and emphasized maximizing [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] firepower rather than achieving starfighter superiority, and it subordinated its starfighters to this role.<ref name="ISB" /> The Navy's earliest [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]] design, the [[Venator-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Venator''-class]], had carried a substantial complement of 420 starfighters to counter the swarms of [[Droid starfighter/Legends|droid starfighters]] deployed by the [[Confederate Navy/Legends|Confederate Navy]] and had proved its worth as both a fighting ship and a carrier, but many Imperial strategists came to think that it would have been more effective if designed for a single role. Subsequent Star Destroyer designs like the hangarless [[Tector-class Star Destroyer|''Tector''-class]] were larger and were built around more powerful reactors, allowing them to carry heavier defenses and weapons and so lessen the effectiveness of starfighter attacks. After a period of experimentation, the Navy settled on the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] as the backbone of the Fleet. It was heavily optimized for fleet combat, carrying only a single [[Fighter wing/Legends|wing]] of 72 starfighters.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

The Clone Wars had demonstrated the effectiveness of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]-capable [[Snubfighter/Legends|snubfighters]]&mdash;heavily armed starfighters capable of both [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfighting]] and dealing damage to capital ships&mdash;as [[Battleship/Legends|battleship]] killers. However, seeing it as a distasteful legacy of the hordes of [[Vulture-class starfighter/Legends|''Vulture''-class droid starfighters]] deployed by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatists]], the Imperial Navy abandoned the development of snubfighters in favor of the more traditional combination of dedicated space superiority fighters and bombers: the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE Series]], which exemplified traditional starfighter doctrine with the [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/LN starfighter]] and the [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE/sa Bomber]], was a series of bare-bones fighter designs built around a ball-shaped cockpit and the revolutionary [[Twin ion engine/Legends|twin ion engine]] design. Seen as complements to Star Destroyers, they served as escorts, scouts, hit-and-fade raiders, and [[Bomber/Legends|bombers]] supporting ground troops. As such, they lacked [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrives]], [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]], or even life-support systems, reducing their mass and giving them great speed and maneuverability, but limiting their survivability and their range.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

==History==
===The New Order===
[[File:Imperialattackcruisers.png|thumb|right|225px|The Imperial Navy inherits the Republic's Star Destroyers.]]
The Imperial Navy was formed from the Republic Navy of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]]. After [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] [[Declaration of a New Order|declared himself]] [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], establishing the first Galactic Empire, he began a campaign of [[Imperialization/Legends|Imperialization]], under which the Republic Navy, now containing the [[Planetary Security Forces]] of individual member worlds,<ref name="TCSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> was renamed the Imperial Navy. Palpatine boosted military budgets for research, development, and recruitment, and with the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi]] gone, gave the Navy a new role. In a famous speech, he called them “heirs to the role abandoned by the Jedi—protectors of the galaxy and its citizens.”<ref name="Rebellion Era Sourcebook">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref> Palpatine's first [[Emperor's purge|purge]] of the Imperial Navy occurred within two weeks into the Empire's rule. A rapid expansion of the number of Naval ships begun near the end of the Clone Wars was further increased.<ref name="DL:TRODV" /> In addition, Palpatine let the Empire have a massive buildup despite the end of the Clone Wars. As such, citizens of many planets were eager to join the then-newly formed Imperial Navy.<ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary" />

During the [[Reconquest of the Rim]], starting in 19 BBY, the bulk of the Imperial fleet was still composed of [[Victory-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Victory''-class]] and ''Venator''-class Star Destroyers, with their fighter squadrons being composed of V-wings and ARC-170s. However, as the pacification continued, the old Republic warships were gradually retired in favor of the ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers, and TIE fighters also flew with other fighters.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

[[File:S5tTZFb.jpg|thumb|left|225px|Imperial Navy recruitment spread.]]

The Reconquest and the clearance of the [[Separatist holdouts/Legends|last holdouts]] of the Confederacy of Independent Systems from the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] was the first campaign of the new Imperial Navy, and would be fondly remembered by Imperial loyalists as a time when the young Empire restored stability and order to the galaxy in the aftermath of the Clone Wars. Through campaigns like the [[Ciutric Offensive]], the [[Sy Myrthian Insurrection]], the [[Five Veils Campaign]], the [[Listehol Campaign]], the [[Noolian Crisis]], and the [[Western Reaches Operation]], Naval officers like [[Terrinald Screed/Legends|Terrinald Screed]], [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]], [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]], and [[Octavian Grant]], as well as starfighter [[Ace/Legends|aces]] like [[Shea Hublin]], became heroes to the Imperial populace.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> At the height of the Empire, in large part because of its reputation of upholding law and order in the known galaxy, Naval officers were often held with respect and admiration, as well as having trillions of personnel in service.<ref name="TRG1" />

The Empire's aggressive militarization continued throughout the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]]. Of the entire Imperial Military, the Navy benefited the most, ultimately swelling to a strength of 25,000 ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers and millions more smaller warships and support vessels by the time of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The numerical size of the Imperial Navy as well as its firepower capabilities were such that even [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]], one of the leaders of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]], acknowledged that what ground the Alliance held mattered little if it could not win the clash of navies. However, it was later remarked by Alliance strategists like [[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]] that the Imperial Navy grew far too fast, resulting in a force that was top-heavy with war machines that it could not effectively crew or repair.<ref name="Handbook" /><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

The continued growth of the Imperial Navy despite the absence of a clear and present danger to the Empire was a factor in the [[Declaration of Rebellion/Legends|Declaration of Rebellion]] in [[2 BBY/Legends|2 BBY]].<ref name="RASB">''[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook]]''</ref> Additionally, a philosophical divide emerged in the Imperial Navy between the "[[Generationals]]"&mdash;those officers whose families had done military service for centuries&mdash;and new up-and-coming officers who tended to be [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] partisans. The Generationals saw the Empire as an improvement on the ideals of the Republic and saw the Navy as a tool for establishing stability and order, and so peace. The true believers of the New Order, however, saw the Old Republic as decrepit and sought to rule by fear, best represented by the policy of state terror set out in the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> The increasingly brutal and arbitrary operations conducted against dissent by the Imperial Navy such as the [[Nembus Sector campaign]] and the [[Kwymar Suppressions/Legends|Kwymar Suppressions]] led many Generational officers to become disillusioned with the Empire.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

===Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|Alert all commands. Deploy the fleet.|Firmus Piett|<ref name="ESB" />}}
[[File:ExecutorEscort-BTMF27.png|thumb|right|225px|The [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], escorted by two Imperial Star Destroyers]]
Growing discontent with the Empire eventually coalesced into the Alliance to Restore the Republic, which began a military campaign against Imperial forces. Many of the Alliance's most senior [[Commander/Legends|commanders]] were in fact disillusioned Imperial Navy officers, among them [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna]] and [[Adar Tallon/Legends|Adar Tallon]], both Imperial heroes of the Sy Myrthian Insurrection during the Reconquest of the Rim.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

In many subsequent engagements, the Navy provided support to the Imperial Army as well as fighting the Alliance ship-to-ship. Although the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]] was not as large or as powerful as the well-trained Imperial Navy, the two fleets would battle each other regularly throughout the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. An early humiliation was dealt to the Imperial Navy by the Alliance at the [[Battle of Turkana/Legends|Battle of Turkana]], and thereafter the Navy faced a serious challenge to its established doctrine: since it lacked large numbers of capital ships, the Rebel Alliance made heavy use of snubfighters as part of its [[stateless strategy]]. Powerful starfighters like the [[BTL-S3 Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL-S3 Y-wing]] and [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing]] conducted [[Hit-and-hype raiding|hit-and-hype raids]] against prominent Imperial targets and supply convoys, using their superior shielding, armament, and hyperdrives to inflict disproportionate damage on Imperial targets. Meanwhile, the Alliance Fleet roamed the galaxy, challenging Imperial authority merely by existing, and waiting for the chance of a decisive battle with the Galactic Empire.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

The Galactic Empire made belated moves to develop their own snubfighters like the [[TIE Advanced x1/Legends|TIE Advanced x1]] and the [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE/D Defender]] after the Rebels inflicted humiliating defeats on them with X-wings, but the most numerous new development was the [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE/IN]], a non-hyperspace-capable traditional [[Interceptor/Legends|interceptor]] that, though capable of outracing Rebel fighters, was not equipped with deflector shields.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> The Navy was present at both [[Death Star/Legends|Death Stars]] and suffered massive losses as a result of the Alliance's destruction of the stations at the Battle of Yavin in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], and the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref><ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

The command structure of the entire Navy was reorganized around 2 BBY with Emperor Palpatine's appointment of the twelve [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]], the most senior officers of the whole Starfleet.<ref name="WW:IGA" /> Widely seen as an attempt by the Emperor to increase his power over the Fleet, Imperial officers swapped numerous conspiracy theories as to the method behind his appointments. The truth of the appointments was that, though all the Grand Admirals were exceptionally gifted officers, they were not just front-line commanders; rather, they included several technical specialists and theoreticians, enabling them to serve as a leadership cadre for the whole Imperial Military — and indeed the whole Empire.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

Though the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first Death Star]] was technically a Navy [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]], many traditionalists and Generationals in the Navy were horrified by the idea of presenting an existential threat to terrorize planets into submission. In addition, the Death Star threatened to eliminate the Navy's prestige as the greatest expression of Imperial power. After the Death Star was destroyed at [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin]] and Wilhuff Tarkin was killed, the Navy championed the [[Sarlacc Project]] and the creation of a new class of massive [[Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnoughts]], which became the Empire's mightiest warships. Designed to be so powerful that the mere threat of their deployment would pacify multiple [[Sector/Legends|sectors]], the first class was the 19,000-meter [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|''Executor''-class Star Dreadnought]], led by the [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] of [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Lord Darth Vader]], the [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']]. [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]], a new Star Destroyer fleet led by Darth Vader, [[Kendal Ozzel/Legends|Kendal Ozzel]] and [[Firmus Piett/Legends|Firmus Piett]] aboard the ''Executor'', dealt the Rebel Alliance a shattering defeat at the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] in [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> The ''Executor''{{'s}} example led to the development of the even more massive, [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]]-equipped [[Sovereign-class Super Star Destroyer|''Sovereign''-]] and [[Eclipse-class dreadnought|''Eclipse''-class]] dreadnoughts, which were intended to revolutionize [[Space warfare/Legends|space warfare]] and ensure Imperial dominance of space for a century.<ref name="Handbook" />

[[File:Imperial_Fleet_at_Endor_FFG.png|thumb|left|250px|The bulk of the Imperial Navy amassed at Endor]]
A few months before the Battle of Endor, one of the Grand Admirals, [[Demetrius Zaarin]], attempted a [[Zaarin insurrection|coup]] against Emperor Palpatine, which was put down by forces led by [[Sith Lord/Legends|Lord]] Darth Vader and the mysterious [[Chiss/Legends|Chiss]] [[Vice Admiral/Legends|Vice Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Mitth'raw'nuruodo]], better known by his [[Core name/Legends|core name]], Thrawn. After Zaarin's death, Thrawn was officially promoted to Grand Admiral as his replacement (although other evidence suggests that the Chiss had, in fact, been promoted in secret at an earlier stage). Thereafter Thrawn was sent to continue his exploration mission in the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]], and he was not present at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]].<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

Around the time of the Battle of Endor in 4 ABY, massive Navy invasion fleets were moving into position near the Rebel redoubts of [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] and the [[Calamari sector/Legends|Calamari sector]]. Emperor Palpatine plotted to trap the Alliance Fleet between the [[Death Star II/Legends|Second Death Star]] and Death Squadron over the Forest Moon of Endor and destroy it, then wait for the Death Star to be completed before obliterating Chandrila and [[Dac/Legends|Dac]] to end the Rebellion for good.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> The plot was a disaster, however. With the assistance of the native [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] of Endor, General [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] destroyed the [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shield]] generator protecting the Death Star and General [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] and Admiral [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] destroyed the Death Star and much of Death Squadron. Darth Vader, Emperor Palpatine and Admiral Piett were killed in the battle, and many of the Empire's most promising young officers died in the destruction of the ''Executor'', which would cripple the Navy's leadership in the years that followed.<ref name="ROTJ" /><ref name="TEGTVAV">''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref> In the absence of clear leadership after the Emperor's death and the ''Executor''{{'s}} loss, [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]] of the Star Destroyer [[Chimaera/Legends|''Chimaera'']] ordered the Imperial fleet to retreat from Endor.<ref name="Thrawn Trilogy">''[[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy]]''</ref>

===Warlordism and decline===
{{Quote|Luke... I'm seeing him. He's commanding the Imperial forces! Like our father! I fear we've lost him, Han. I fear we've lost everything.|Leia Organa Solo, sensing her brother taking command of the Imperial Navy|<ref name="Dark Empire 2" />}}
When no decisive leadership emerged after the defeat at Endor, the Galactic Empire split up into warring factions led by [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]], and the Imperial Navy splintered along with it. Warlord fiefdoms like [[Ardus Kaine]]'s [[Pentastar Alignment]], [[Treuten Teradoc]]'s [[Greater Maldrood]], [[Blitzer Harrsk]]'s [[Zero Command]], and the [[Zsinj's Empire|empire]] of Grand Moff [[Zsinj]] took cuts of the fleet, while only a Loyalist rump remained to protect the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Imperial Ruling Council]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] led by [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]].<ref name="Atlas" /> The Imperial Navy's ability to fight was further reduced by the [[Alliance of Free Planets]]' [[Defense Declarations]], which proclaimed the Alliance's intent to devolve control of the Planetary Security Forces, nationalized into the Navy's [[Sector Group/Legends|Sector Groups]] by the Empire, back to the sectors. Loyal Imperial Sector Groups dismissed the measure as illegal, but for others the Declarations caused many sectors that had been on the edge to side with the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. Other sectors divided over whether to accept the Declarations, fomenting further warlordism and infighting and significantly reducing the number of enemies the Alliance had to fight.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

While capable Loyalist officers like [[Llon Banjeer]], [[Uther Kermen]], and Gilad Pellaeon resisted the New Republic's advance into the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]], engaging them in savage battles at [[Milagro campaign|Milagro]], [[Battle of Mindor|Mindor]], and [[Battle of Denon (Galactic Civil War)|Denon]], they were ultimately unable to prevent Admiral Ackbar from [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|capturing Coruscant]] in [[6 ABY/Legends|6 ABY]]. Thereafter, the personal ambition of warlords caused the Imperial Navy's strength to collapse further, particularly after the Loyalist Admiral [[Teren Rogriss]] ''de facto'' allied with the New Republic to destroy both Warlord Zsinj and Treuten Teradoc, who had been raiding both Imperial and New Republic targets. In the [[Post–Zsinj campaigns|campaigns that followed]], the Empire lost yet more of its military forces owing to New Republic attacks and infighting, its [[Kuat Drive Yards/Legends|premier shipyard]] with the Republic [[Taking of Kuat|capture]] of [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]], and the prestigious Core World of [[Anaxes/Legends|Anaxes]], the "Defender of the Core" and the site of the [[Republic Navy War College/Legends|Navy War College]].<ref name="Chronology">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /><ref name="Atlas" />

[[File:Byssfleet1.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The [[Byss Defense Fleet]] was the tool of the Reborn Emperor's reconquest.]]
By [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], [[Imperial Space]] had been pushed back to a bare quarter of its former territory in the Outer Rim, and the loyalty of much of the Fleet was uncertain. However, the Imperial Navy was briefly reunified after Mitth'raw'nuruodo, "the thirteenth Grand Admiral," re-emerged from the Unknown Regions. With Gilad Pellaeon as his second-in-command, Grand Admiral Thrawn fought a [[Thrawn campaign|brilliant military campaign]] that reconquered nearly half the known galaxy for the Empire until his sudden death at the [[Battle of Bilbringi (9 ABY)|Battle of Bilbringi]].<ref name="Atlas" /><ref name="Thrawn Trilogy" />

Inspired by Thrawn's example, the warlords of the Outer Rim and the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] unified and began [[Pre–Shadow Hand campaign|their own campaign]] against the New Republic. Three enormous Imperial task forces advanced out of the Deep Core, anchored around four ''Executor''-class dreadnoughts, five [[Mandator III-class dreadnought|''Mandator'' III-class dreadnoughts]], and three [[Vengeance-class dreadnought|''Vengeance''-class dreadnoughts]], [[Battle of Kaikielius (Galactic Civil War)|conquering Kaikielius]] and [[Battle of Alsakan (Galactic Civil War)|Alsakan]] while fleets out of the [[New Territories/Legends|New Territories]] [[Second Battle of Coruscant|reconquered Coruscant]]. Much of the unified Navy's strength was lost in the subsequent [[Imperial Civil War]], however, laying much of Coruscant to waste and spreading across much of the recaptured galaxy. The Star Dreadnoughts ''[[Whelm]]'' and ''[[Panthac]]'' destroyed each other over [[Alsakan/Legends|Alsakan]]; the Captain of the ''Vengeance''-class dreadnought [[Javelin (Vengeance-class)|''Javelin'']] rammed his ship into a [[Unidentified Torpedo Sphere (Chasin)|Torpedo Sphere]] defending [[Chasin]], and squadrons of [[TIE/D automated starfighter|droid TIE Fighters]] destroyed the ''Mandator'' III-class dreadnought ''[[Aculeus]]'' at [[Drearia/Legends|Drearia]].<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /><ref name="Dark Empire">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref>

The madness of the Imperial Civil War was soon revealed to have been encouraged by Emperor Palpatine, who had used the power of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]] to preserve his spirit after Endor and had been reborn in a [[Cloning/Legends|clone]] body. After using the Civil War to solidify his rule, the Reborn Emperor launched [[Operation Shadow Hand]], a savage series of battles against the New Republic, with [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapons]] such as the [[World Devastator]]s, the [[Galaxy Gun]], and the ''Eclipse''-class dreadnought equipping the Imperial Navy. Despite violent engagements at [[Battle of Pinnacle Base|Da Soocha V]] and [[Battle of Calamari|Dac]], however, Palpatine was ultimately defeated for good on [[Battle of Onderon (Galactic Civil War)|Onderon]] by the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Empatojayos Brand]], and [[Eclipse II|his flagship]] was destroyed after the [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] forced it to fly into the Galaxy Gun orbiting [[Byss/Legends|Byss]].<ref name="Dark Empire" /><ref name="Chronology" />

Imperial authority briefly continued in the Outer Rim after Palpatine's final death in the form of the [[Crimson Empire]], led by the traitorous [[Emperor's Royal Guard/Legends|Imperial Royal Guard]] [[Carnor Jax]]. However, after Jax and his successor, [[Xandel Carivus]], were killed by [[Kir Kanos]], the last of the Royal Guards, utter collapse of Imperial authority followed, Imperial Space reduced to squabbling warlord factions, [[Moff/Legends|Moffs]] and governors, and [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress worlds]]. The Imperial Navy effectively ceased to exist.<ref name="Crimson Empire">''[[Star Wars: Crimson Empire]]''</ref><ref name="Chronology" /><ref name="Atlas" />

===Imperial Reunification===
[[File:LusankyavsReaper-EGW.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The [[Orinda campaign]] was one of the few victories of the post-Palpatine Imperial Navy.]]
The Imperial Navy was at last [[Imperial Reunification|reunified]] in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] under Admiral Natasi Daala, once lover and protégé of Wilhuff Tarkin, who murdered the warlords of the Deep Core and consolidated their forces under her command. Daala took Grand Admiral Thrawn's former second-in-command, Vice Admiral Gilad Pellaeon, as her chief lieutenant. After she was defeated in an [[Assault on Yavin 4|attack]] on the [[Jedi Praxeum]] at [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. Daala promoted Pellaeon to full Admiral and surrendered command of Imperial forces to him.<ref name="Darksaber">[[Darksaber (novel)|''Darksaber'']]</ref> Pellaeon stripped the Deep Core of all Imperial fleet assets and withdrew to the New Territories. There he formed alliances with the Moffs, building a powerful fleet around the Deep Core dreadnoughts ''[[Megador]]'' and [[Dominion (Star Dreadnought)|''Dominion'']], and Ardus Kaine's ''Executor''-class [[Reaper (Executor-class)|''Reaper'']]. With this force, Pellaeon established an official [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] in the Outer Rim.<ref name="Chronology" /><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

With the unified Imperial Navy at his command, Pellaeon launched the [[Orinda campaign]] in 12 ABY, reconquering [[Orinda/Legends|Orinda]]. After a month of fighting, the [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]] was dealt a humbling defeat at the [[Battle of Orinda]]: Pellaeon used the ''Reaper'' to fix the New Republic dreadnought ''[[Lusankya/Legends|Lusankya]]'' in the system, while the fleet carrier [[Endurance (Endurance-class)|''Endurance'']] was delayed in launching its [[E-7 E-wing multi-role starfighter|E-wings]]. ''Endurance'' was destroyed with the majority of her fighter complement still on board when the ''Dominion'', kept secretly in reserve by Pellaeon, arrived in-system behind six [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Interdictor cruisers]].<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

The Orinda campaign secured the Remnant's southern border, but Pellaeon's gains were squandered over the next five years by the Remnant's Moffs. An [[Galactic Civil War/Legends#The Borderlands Campaign|ill-conceived offensive]] into the [[Trans-Hydian/Legends|Trans-Hydian]] resulted in the destruction of the ''Reaper'' at the [[Battle of Celanon]] in [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]]. An attempt to take advantage of the New Republic's apparent disarray after the [[Black Fleet Crisis]] in [[17 ABY/Legends|17 ABY]] was an utter disaster for the Imperial Navy: Pellaeon managed to [[Battle of Adumar (17 ABY)|take Adumar]] and won surprise attacks on [[First battle of Taris|Taris]] and [[Battle of Champala|Champala]] on the [[Hydian Way/Legends|Hydian Way]], pushing all the way to the edge of the Core Worlds, but after Admiral Ackbar and General [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]] brought the full weight of the [[New Republic Defense Force/Legends|New Republic Defense Force]] to bear, the [[Second Battle of Champala]] became an Imperial rout. The Imperial Navy was chased back to Imperial Space, which was rapidly reduced after defeats at [[Ketaris/Legends|Ketaris]] and [[Tangrene]], and the [[Battle of Anx Minor]] was a disaster, with the ''Megador'' and ''Dominion'' suffering severe damage. Pellaeon ordered an immediate retreat to [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]].<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> In mere weeks the Imperial Remnant had been reduced to a rump of eight Outer Rim sectors, and a navy that had numbered in the millions was reduced to mere thousands, with just two hundred Star Destroyers remaining. The eight remaining sectors were so heavily militarized that Pellaeon was able to make the New Republic agree to a [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty|conditional peace]] in [[19 ABY/Legends|19 ABY]], formally ending the Galactic Civil War,<ref name="SOTP">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref> but it would take more than a century before the Imperial Navy was restored to its former glory.<ref name="SWL0½" />

===Yuuzhan Vong War and aftermath===
The Imperial Navy would once again became a veritable fighting force participating under Pellaeon's command in the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]]. The Remnant's Navy was still considered an extremely powerful force for the territory it controlled by [[40 ABY/Legends|40 ABY]], and it continued weapons research with the development of the [[Turbulent-class Star Destroyer|''Turbulent''-class "Pocket Star Destroyer"]]. Both the [[Confederation]] and the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances courted the support of the Remnant's fleets during the Second Galactic Civil War.<ref name="LOTF">''[[Star Wars: Legacy of the Force]]''</ref> After the ascension of [[Jagged Fel]] to the position of [[Head of State (Imperial Remnant)|Head of State]], the Remnant's Navy came to include [[Chiss Star Destroyer]]s and [[Nssis-class Clawcraft|''Nssis''-class Clawcraft]] owing to Fel's links to the Chiss through Grand Admiral Thrawn's old [[Empire of the Hand]].<ref name="Ascension">''[[Fate of the Jedi: Ascension]]''</ref>

===Fel and Sith regimes===
{{Quote|We swore oaths of duty to the throne and that throne is on Coruscant. We pledged our lives and our honor to this duty!|[[Vaclen Tor]]|<ref name="Legacy 36">[[Legacy (2006) 36|''Legacy'' (2006) 36]]</ref>}}
[[File:ralltiir_battle_second_imperial_civil_war.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The [[Core Fleet|Galactic Alliance Core Fleet]] and the Fel loyalist [[Bastion Second Fleet]] engage the Sith loyal [[Coruscant Third Fleet]] at the [[Battle of Ralltiir (Second Imperial Civil War)|Battle of Ralltiir]], [[137 ABY]].]]
The Imperial Navy would regain much of its former strength by the time of the [[Fel Empire]], when Jagged Fel and [[Fel dynasty|his descendants]] claimed the title of Emperor. Under the Fels, it fought the Galactic Alliance in the [[Sith–Imperial War]] of [[127 ABY|127]]-[[130 ABY]]. By this time, nearly all of the Imperial Navy's arsenal had been replaced. Large battleships had been abandoned almost entirely, though the Navy still favored the Star Destroyer with the [[Pellaeon-class Star Destroyer|''Pellaeon''-class]] as its main capital warship. However, it did not build any larger warships beyond the prototype [[Imperious-class Star Destroyer|''Imperious''-class Star Destroyer]]. Smaller, lighter warships like the [[Ardent-class fast frigate|''Ardent''-class fast frigate]] were more common in its fleets than in the Imperial Period. The [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Navy Starfighter Corps]] continued to prefer the ancient combination of interceptors and bombers, with the heavily shielded, Chiss-inspired [[Predator-class fighter|''Predator''-class fighter]] and the [[Neutralizer-class bomber|''Neutralizer''-class bomber]] filling its forces.<ref name="Legacy">''[[Star Wars: Legacy]]''</ref>

After the [[One Sith]] led by [[Darth Krayt]] and the [[Council of Moffs/Legends|Council of Moffs]] betrayed Emperor [[Roan Fel]] in 130 ABY and unsuccessfully attempted to assassinate him, the Imperial Navy would be split between followers of [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire]] and loyalists of the [[Empire-in-exile]] in the subsequent [[Second Imperial Civil War]]. The faction of the Navy loyal to the Fel dynasty sided with the [[Galactic Alliance Remnant]] led by Admiral [[Gar Stazi]] after the [[Battle of Mon Calamari (Second Imperial Civil War)|Battle of Dac]], and in [[138 ABY]] successfully [[Battle of Coruscant (Second Imperial Civil War)|defeated]] the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] at Coruscant and restored the Fel dynasty with the proclamation of Roan Fel's daughter [[Marasiah Fel|Marasiah]] as Empress.<ref name="Legacy" />

==Organization==
===Headquarters===
Prior to the Battle of Endor and the ''de facto'' collapse of Imperial authority, the highest organizational body of the Imperial Military was the [[Imperial High Command/Legends|Imperial High Command]]. Below this was [[Naval Command (Imperial)|Naval Command]] and the [[Admiralty (Imperial)/Legends|Admiralty]], the organizing body that directed all operations of the Imperial Navy. Naval Command took orders directly from Emperor Palpatine.<ref name="Handbook" /> The [[Commander Fleet Operations]] had a high enough rank to both oversee various navy operations<ref name="Base of Operations">{{SWGTCG|set=Agents of Deception|cardname=Base of Operations}}</ref> and affix SpecPlates to various Imperial vessels that qualified.<ref name="SpecPlate">[["Imperial Star Destroyer" SpecPlate]]</ref> On rare occasions, Naval Command also had direct involvement in military operations.<ref name="The Constancia Affair">"[[The Constancia Affair]]"</ref>

The [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]], [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] - whose title was also styled as "Commander of the Imperial Fleet" - exercised supreme control over the Imperial Navy,<ref name="kenner" /> with his orders being placed on the same priority as Emperor Palpatine's own instructions.<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook2">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> The next-in-line authority was the cadre of the [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]], a body of senior naval officers known also as the "Circle of Twelve". The promotions were generally seen as an attempt by the Emperor to solidify his control over the Navy. Comprising respected naval strategists, researchers, and New Order partisans, they were assembled to be a leadership cadre for the entire Imperial Military.<ref name="Handbook" /><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

===Administration===
Within Naval Command, the Navy was administrated by four organizational branches: the [[Line Branch]], the [[Flight Branch]], the [[Fleet Support Branch]], and the [[Support Service Branch]]. Each of these organizational branches had divisions that focused on specific areas in the Imperial Navy.<ref name="Handbook" />

The Line Branch was responsible for the Empire's [[Warship/Legends|warships]], capital ships, and support ships, as well as their commanders and crew. It was tasked with handling strategy, tactics, and administration within the Naval forces. It housed various divisions, the three largest being the [[Deck Division]], the [[Logistics Division/Legends|Logistics Division]], and the [[Administration Division]].<ref name="Handbook" /> Line officers commanded bridge crews, captained ships, and commanded [[Fleet/Legends|fleets]].<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

The Flight Branch oversaw the operations of combat starships. It had various smaller divisions and one large division known as the [[Flight Division]], which held direct command over the [[Starfighter Corps (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Starfighter Corps]] of the Empire, including the Empire's [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]], [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]], and support crew.<ref name="Handbook" /> The Flight Branch held purview over the [[Navy Order of Battle]].

The Fleet Support Branch consisted of officers responsible for maintenance and engineering duties. This branch had two divisions: [[Engineering Division]] and [[Technical Services Division]].<ref name="Handbook" /> The former focused on maintaining various Navy ships' sublight and hyperspace engines, as well as the integrity of the ships' hulls. The latter looked after power distribution, life support, and other specialties outside the Engineering Division's jurisdiction.

The Support Service Branch provided services to allow Navy personnel to carry out their duties. It had at least five branches: [[Ordnance]], [[Gunnery]], [[Communications]], [[Biological]], and [[Astrogation (section)|Astrogation]].<ref name="Handbook" /> Ordnance dealt with the installation and maintenance of various naval ships' weapons systems. Gunnery supplied personnel to man the weapons systems. Communications controlled traffic and handled information systems. Biological handled research and provided medical services, and Astrogation calculated hyperspace routes alongside other navigation-related matters.

In addition to these four main branches, there were several divisions within the Imperial Navy. One was the [[Imperial Navy Intelligence]], which dealt with intelligence-gathering activities. Another was the Navy's secret elite force, known as the [[Imperial Naval Special Forces]]. The [[Imperial Navy Research, Development and Engineering Center]] was responsible for developing new Imperial warships at least since prior to the Battle of Endor. The [[Imperial Naval Special Forces|special forces]] carried out special operations for the Navy on foot. [[Imperial Supply]] may have been a division in the Imperial Navy, due to the Academy system's Rhinnal academy supplying training for both [[Merchant Galactic/Legends|Merchant Services]] (the civilian auxiliary to the Imperial Navy) and the Imperial Supply Fleet. As a result, even though it was technically civilian in nature, the Merchant Services had indirect ties to the Imperial Navy.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> Although technically being support branches of the Imperial Military overall, the [[Imperial Exploration Corps/Legends|Imperial Exploration Corps]] and the [[Imperial Survey Corps/Legends|Imperial Survey Corps]] were attached to the Imperial Navy, with the Navy utilizing both groups' studies to determine which worlds to conquer and exploit, although they generally did this without the knowledge of the members of both corps.<ref name="Handbook" /> The [[Emperor's special reserve guard]] was an elite force of starfighter pilots that were presumably tasked with aiding the Emperor.<ref name="Star Wars: TIE Fighter">[[Star Wars: TIE Fighter (video game)|''Star Wars: TIE Fighter'']]</ref>

The Imperial Navy conducted itself by the [[Imperial Naval Code]], a set of martial laws and regulations created to guide the massive military organization. The Naval Code encouraged unquestioning obedience to orders and stressed a willingness to die for the Empire.<ref name="Handbook" />

===Tactical organization===
[[File:Imperial_Fleet.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Part of the fleet]]
{{Main|Navy Order of Battle}}
{{Quote|You don't have an organization, admiral! What you have is nothing like the Army!''"<br />"''Yes, general, the Army has its organization. We in the Navy must content ourselves with the control of all known space.|An Imperial Army general and a Navy admiral|<ref name="ISB2" />}}
The Imperial Navy's tactical organization was defined by the Navy Order of Battle, designed to provide flexible resources for a commander's force requirements.<ref name="Handbook" />

The Imperial Navy's largest formal organizational unit was the Sector Group, nominally composed of 2,600 starships, of which 24 were ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers and another 1,600 were smaller warships, under the control of a [[High Admiral]], usually the sector Moff.<ref name="Handbook" /> The Sector Groups were split into multiple fleets of around 400 ships each led by [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admirals]], with the Group's combat elements being split between "Superiority" and "Escort." A [[superiority fleet]] was a space-combat force spearheaded by six Star Destroyers, each nominally accompanied by a [[battle squadron]] of eighteen smaller ships. While superiority fleets were officially assigned to fleet combat, in practice they were normally used as mobile reserves, projecting Imperial power in response to local threats. Escort fleets, meanwhile, were composed of [[force escort]]s and were designated for combat against pirates and raiders, which in practice meant that they were the Empire's first line of defense, protecting civilian [[Freighter/Legends|freighters]], attacking corsairs' hideouts, and guarding remote outposts. Additional fleet commands were established for the Sector Group's logistics and support forces, including [[Assault fleet|troop transport]], [[Bombard fleet|bombardment]], [[Deepdock fleet|deepdock]] and [[support fleet]]s.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> Han Solo, when witnessing [[the Graveyard]] for the first time, implied that an Imperial fleet composed of a thousand starships with a significant amount of firepower would have been sufficient in doing at least significant damage to a planet.<ref name="ANH" />

Below the level of fleet was the [[systems force]], led by an admiral appointed as its [[Commodore/Legends|Commodore]]. Systems forces totaled around ninety ships in several [[Squadron/Legends|squadrons]], and included [[force superiority]] designed to maintain control of space in calm areas; force escort to protect commercial shipments and convoys; [[System bombard|systems bombard]] to carry out planetary bombardments with [[Torpedo Sphere/Legends|Torpedo Spheres]]; and [[transport force]]s, [[force technical services]], and [[force support]] to supply combat formations.<ref name="Handbook" /> In practice, however, despite their nominal strength, most systems forces contained only a single combat squadron.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

Squadrons of 14 to 60 ships were the smallest independent operational units of the Navy, and were designated as [[Light squadron|light]], [[Heavy squadron|heavy]], battle, or [[Bombard squadron|bombard]] squadrons. Battle squadrons built around an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer were the core components of superiority fleets, and were nominally supported by three [[Line of battle|lines]] of eighteen smaller ships. In practice, Star Destroyers were normally accompanied by just two or three escorts, if any: the ''Imperial''-class was designed to operate without support, and its hyperdrive was too fast for any escorts except for the speediest light cruisers. The battle squadron was used for offensive operations against a known enemy, and the mere arrival of an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer was often enough to put down a planetary revolt or scare off an armed space-threat.<ref name="Handbook" /><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

[[File:PlanetaryBombardment-SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|right|220px|A fleet consisting of ''Executor''-class Dreadnoughts, ''Imperial''-class Destroyers and Nebulon-B frigates conduct an [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombardment]].]]

The most basic combat formation in the Imperial Navy was the line of battle, or simply a line, and the smallest organizational unit used for space combat. The Imperial Starfleet shaped four to twenty starships into lines, depending on type. The line was the most amorphous level of organization in the Starfleet. The Imperial Starfleet Order of Battle outlined seven types of lines: [[Attack line|attack]], [[Heavy attack line|heavy attack]], [[Recon line|reconnaissance]], [[Pursuit line|pursuit]], [[Skirmish line|skirmish]], [[Troop line|troop]] and [[Torpedo line|torpedo]].<ref name="Handbook" /> In addition to the seven types of lines, the Imperial Navy considered an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer a line in itself. While an ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer may have been able to act as an attack line and its complement of starfighters as a skirmish line, the decision to give commanders the option to field a ship equivalent to a heavy cruiser as a line unto itself was more political than tactical. After a naval staff study suggested a Star Destroyer was the field equivalent of the smallest of naval squadrons, the Admiralty decided that, as there were more lines than squadrons, designating the Star Destroyer as a line unit would get them more Star Destroyers. The Admiralty's thinking prevailed.

A full ten percent of the entire Imperial Navy was kept in reserve in the Core Worlds, so as to be able to quickly respond to threats throughout the galaxy.<ref name="SWSB">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> A [[Outer Rim Imperial Fleet|fleet]] with at least 19 ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyers and three Immobilizer 418 cruisers, the latter supplied by [[Imperial Drydock IV]], was also kept permanently in the Outer Rim Territories.<ref name="X-wing">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref>

Roving fleets aimed at specific tasks were fielded at several points in Imperial history. Notable units included Death Squadron<ref name="ISB" /><ref name="RASB" /> and [[Scourge Squadron]],<ref name="TPA">{{JournalCite|3|The Pentastar Alignment}}</ref> which hunted for Rebel bases in the Outer Rim. There was also the [[Vengeance Battle Group]], used by the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]] to search for the [[Valley of the Jedi]],<ref name="DF:JK">''[[Dark Forces: Jedi Knight]]''</ref> and the [[secret armada]] assembled by Admiral [[Mils Giel]], for the purpose of transporting a vital biological device from the Outer Rim to Imperial Center.<ref name="SW60">[[Star Wars (1977) 60|''Star Wars'' (1977) 60]]</ref> At least one [[Star Destroyer task force]] was used to punish Imperial sectors that threatened to undermine Imperial rule, as when the [[Moff (Trans-Nebular sector)|Moff]] of the [[Trans-Nebular sector/Legends|Trans-Nebular sector]] established himself as the de facto warlord and was engaged by a fleet of Star Destroyers. This force was large enough to leave behind vessels that would form the core of a new sector fleet, before moving on to other trouble spots.<ref name="GSOTE">''[[Goroth: Slave of the Empire]]''</ref> A fleet stationed near Byss was formed since the start of the Galactic Empire. The Emperor also possessed a [[Emperor's fleet|personal fleet]] that he commanded, utilizing it in situations important enough to require his personal participation.

==Personnel==
===Specializations===
[[File:Imperial_Ensign.jpg|thumb|left|200px|An Imperial [[Ensign/Legends|ensign]]]]
Although the main ships of the Imperial Navy were important, the manpower was also vitally important within the navy. Like most militaries, the Imperial Navy divided its personnel into [[Imperial officer/Legends|officers]] and enlisted.

Officers held command appointments over ships, fleets or bridge crews. The Empire's Core-centric political rule almost invariably gave positions of high command to Core Worlders, and lack of powerful connections within the military hierarchy could be a bar to high rank. A notable exception to this was the career of Firmus Piett of [[Axxila/Legends|Axxila]], who rose from humble beginnings in the [[Ciutric Hegemony]] to become the Admiral of Darth Vader's Death Squadron. Officers tended to be highly [[Humanocentrism|Humanocentric]] and fully supportive of the New Order's anti-alien policies.<ref name="Handbook" /><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /><ref name="Complete Visual Dictionary" />

The enlisted ranks comprised the Navy's specialists, security personnel, and [[Technician/Legends|technicians]]. [[Imperial Navy crewman|Imperial Navy crewmen]] manned ship stations and maintained systems, monitoring the various instruments on various vessels. Crewmen often worked in sunken pits on the bridge, ostensibly to keep them focused on their work, but also as an intimidation measure. The [[Imperial Navy Trooper/Legends|Naval Troopers]] of the [[Imperial Fleet Regiment]]s maintained security aboard ship and repelled boarding actions. Responsible for manning the Navy's weapon emplacements, the [[Imperial gunner/Legends|Imperial gunners]] were a specialized corps of Flight Branch composed of men who had failed piloting exams but nonetheless possessed keen eyes, superior reflexes, and a rapport with specialized equipment.<ref name="Handbook" /><ref name="DSOwner'sManual>''[[Death Star Owner's Technical Manual]]''</ref>

Imperial pilots came under the aegis of Flight Branch and the Starfighter Corps. The [[TIE pilot]]s were the elite of Flight Branch, and formed their own unique social group within the Navy. The Empire at its height produced millions of TIE pilots, and generally considered them expendable assets.<ref name="Handbook" /> Other pilots included the [[Cruisemissile trooper]]s, who acted as pilots of the [[Cruisemissile assault craft]].

The Navy maintained its own special forces: [[Imperial Navy commando]]s and [[Imperial Naval Special Forces|SpecNav Force troopers]] were elite forces within the Imperial Navy. Occasionally, the Emperor's Royal Guard would participate in Imperial Navy formations.

The [[Stormtrooper Corps/Legends|Stormtrooper Corps]] was not part of the Navy, but [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] were deployed aboard warships to ensure loyalty.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> The [[Imperial Marines/Legends|Imperial Marines]] were a specialized division of the Corps, identified by orange [[Pauldron/Legends|pauldrons]] on their right shoulders, optimized for boarding actions and shipboard combat.<ref name="BF2">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref>

Under the [[Non-huMan]] rule, the vast majority of personnel in the Imperial Starfleet were male [[Human/Legends|Humans]]. Fewer than one precent were not Human. Nevertheless, some Human females, such as Admiral Daala, rose to the high rank, and rare non-Humans could be found in command positions—most famously the Chiss Grand Admiral Thrawn—or as special adjuncts to the usual crew.<ref name="RECG" />

===Training===
{{Main|Imperial Academy/Legends}}
[[File:Prefsbelt_Academy.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The Naval Academy on [[Prefsbelt IV/Legends|Prefsbelt IV]] had trained Midshipmen for millennia.]]
{{Quote|Our credo is 'Service. Fealty. Fidelity.' This may be the first time you have heard it. By the time you graduate, it is one you will never forget.|Fleet Admiral [[Bannidge Holt]] during Imperial Naval Academy cadet indoctrination speech|<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook" />}}
Naval [[Cadet/Legends|cadets]], also known as [[Midshipman/Legends|midshipmen]]<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> and [[crewman-cadet]]s,<ref name="ISB" /><ref name="ISB2" /> began their applications at the [[Star system/Legends|system]] level, attending regional military prep schools. The best students of these schools were invited to attend [[Sector Naval Academy|Sector Naval Academies]], where they completed basic training, learned military history and courtesies, and took examinations to determine what naval career would suit them best.<ref name="TRG1" /><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> The Sector Naval Academies were so named to differentiate them from the primary Naval Academy, and often groomed the best of a stationed world's inhabitants for local and Imperial military careers.<ref name="ISB2" /> Upon arriving at the Sector Naval Academies, their first step in training was attending one of several [[fleet camp]]s spread across the galaxy.<ref name="ISB" /><ref name="ISB2" /> [[Screening Officer]] at the local [[Imperial Recruitment Center]] would then review the cadet's application and decide the type and duration of the cadet's training program.<ref name="TRG1" /><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> Few passed basic training due to the stringent physical and mental requirements. Courses for those who met basic entry included training for piloting both small and large spacecraft, engineering, computer usage, navigation, and medicine, among others. Desired qualities for admission included toughness, bravery, loyalty, and intelligence.<ref name="TRG1" /> Those with the appropriate personality profile were eagerly accepted into the ranks. Those recruits who were both highly rated and already had pilot's certification were considered special interest candidates for Starfighter training.<ref name="ISB2" />

The most promising Naval recruits would be invited to attend officer training at the [[Imperial Naval Academy/Legends|Imperial Naval Academy]] on [[Prefsbelt IV/Legends|Prefsbelt IV]].<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> Such recruits rated within the top two percent of their qualifying tests, and required an endorsement from the local Moff and a more thorough background investigation than other officer candidates. The Academy's location was officially classified, in order to prevent the Academy and any classified secrets from being accessed by anyone aligned with the Rebels or other insurgents, and/or who was politically questionable.<ref name="ISB2" /> It taught midshipmen tactical simulations and leadership before assigning them to active service rotations as [[Ensign/Legends|ensigns]]. Most cadets entered Naval service after a three-year course at Prefsbelt, but some did shorter courses before shifting to [[Flight school/Legends|flight school]] or continuing their studies at one of the three advanced academies.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> For the latter, while the top third of the class could qualify for flight due to the tough entrance requirements and extensive training offered at the Imperial Naval Academy, only those who graduated among the top 5 percent of their class would qualify for actual flight training, while the remaining top third of the class qualified for flight-based specialties such as astrogation, weapons systems, and various other support skills. The academic standards were stringent, with its training methods being the most advanced of their kind, as the Academy system was designed to instill loyalty, build discipline, and develop team interdependence. It was reputed that the greatest of the various naval commanders and Starfighter pilots came from the Academy, with graduation considered an essential step for being promoted to the highest echelons of naval command.<ref name="ISB2" /> Those who showed particular promise by staying for at least five years at the Imperial Naval Academy and demonstrating the desired leadership qualities were eligible for entering [[Officer's Candidacy Training]], which would result in their potentially commanding a strategic outpost, a TIE squadron, or even a Star Destroyer. It was said that the only limits to an officer advancing in the ranks were the officer's inherent ambition, skill, and loyalty.<ref name="TRG1" /> Many of the potential officers came from regional or sector military schools. Courses for officers, which lasted for one standard year, included military indoctrination, education in technical specialties, and training cruises, with crew-man graduates upon graduating being commissioned as a [[Lieutenant/Legends|lieutenant]] and continuing to advanced technical training. Overall, it required 30 months of rigorous physical and academic training, with those graduating afterwards receiving a commission for the rank of lieutenant, and if selected for flight school being expected to complete the more rigorous training with the same degree of excellence.<ref name="ISB2" />

The three specialized military schools were the [[Corulag Academy]], the [[Carida Academy/Legends|Academy of Carida]], and the [[Republic Navy War College/Legends|War College]] on Anaxes. [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]] provided additional training to Navy Midshipmen, Army Cadets, flight school pilots, and specialists from all Imperial services, with an emphasis on active training. The War College, based at [[Anaxes Citadel]], had been considered the embodiment of naval tradition for centuries, and offered active training and combat simulations. It also served as a think tank for promising cadets and active-duty Imperial officers, and tested new warships and equipment for the Navy in training cruises. Finally, the Academy of Carida was a major stormtrooper training facility, and numerous Army, Navy and flight school cadets also spent semesters there. Carida also housed the [[Officer's Candidate School]].<ref name="Handbook" /><ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

Noncommissioned officers and recent graduates of the Imperial Naval College could participate in a training program through the [[Imperial Navy Command Officer's School|Imperial Navy Officers' School]] to focus on military customs and courtesies, military history, leadership, officership, deck command exercises, discipline drills, and other pertinent areas of education of potential officers. Upon graduation, trainees were commissioned in the Imperial Navy as lieutenants. Graduation ceremonies were occasions of great solemnity, pomp and circumstance: "[[The Imperial March (Martial music)|The Imperial March]]," the Navy's martial theme, would be played as new graduates were inducted into the Navy.<ref name="Paradise Snare">''[[The Paradise Snare]]''</ref>

Aside from the main military forces of the Imperial Navy, the academy system also contained the [[Imperial Merchant Galactic Academy]], based on [[Rhinnal/Legends|Rhinnal]], which trained prospective members of the [[Merchant Galactic/Legends|Merchant Services]], an auxiliary branch of the Imperial Navy manned by civilians for transporting supplies and goods, as well as training academies for both the [[Imperial Survey Corps/Legends|Imperial Survey Corps]] and the [[Imperial Exploration Corps/Legends|Imperial Exploration Corps]] (the former at the [[Imperial Exploration Academy]] in the [[Vanik system/Legends|Vanik system]]).<ref name="NPR">[[Star Wars: The National Public Radio Dramatization|''Star Wars'': The National Public Radio Dramatization]]</ref><ref name="Fight for Justice">''[[Star Wars Journal: The Fight for Justice]]''</ref> However, neither academy was considered as prestigious as the Prefsbelt IV academy or the Raithal academy for the Imperial Army.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

===Ranks===
[[File:ImperialNavyRankGuide-EGTW.png|thumb|left|400px|Imperial Navy Rank Guide. Horizontal lines that do not align in the "Plack" section indicate where the relationship between position and rank could vary.]]
{{Main|Rank insignia plaque/Legends}}
Rank within the Imperial Navy was designated by [[Rank insignia plaque/Legends|rank insignia plaques]], breast badges that displayed different combinations of [[Color/Legends|colored]] squares depending on rank. Rank was further denoted by the number of [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]] displayed in pockets near the shoulders of the uniform. The Navy's original rank insignia system used a complex arrangement of red, blue and yellow squares on rank plaques. This was re-organized shortly before the Battle of Yavin in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] in favor of a simpler combination of two rows of blue and red squares only on the plaque, the number of squares increasing with higher rank.<ref name="Handbook" /> However, a number of officers, in particular the [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]], continued to wear the older rank insignia.

The Navy divided rank into ''Position'', ''Line rank'', and ''Specialist rank''. ''Position'' referred to an officer's current assignment on a ship as opposed to permanent rank, and included the honorary titles of High Admiral and [[Warlord of the Empire]], usually granted to [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moffs]] and Grand Admirals. Officers in the position of Lieutenant and ship's Captain wore a single code cylinder with their uniforms, while flag officers wore up to four, the additional cylinders relating to their fleet responsibilities.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" /> A significant change in the Imperial Navy's command structure after being formed was the inclusion of intermediate levels of command, which originally did not exist in the Republic Navy. This resulted in a large number of junior officers being promoted to these intermediate levels. Senior officers generally kept their ranks, but their scope of command had enlarged. For example, an admiral of the Imperial Navy commanded over ten times the force size as a Republic Navy admiral had.<ref name="ISB2" />

''Line ranks'' were permanent ranks held by those who commanded the bridge crew, captained ships, and flew their flags over fleets. Few officers had permanent line ranks above that of Navy [[Captain of the Line/Legends|Senior Captain]]. Although in theory, the rank plaque was associated with line rank, officers in the position of [[Fleet Admiral/Legends|Fleet Admiral]] and ship's captain always wore the insignia of a full admiral and a Senior Captain, respectively. Officers aboard ship who were not in command were addressed as Lieutenants (or in the case of Ensigns, Midshipmen), regardless of their actual rank.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

''Specialist rank'' was held by personnel of the Flight, Support, and Engineering branches and broadly mirrored the line ranks of the [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial Army]]. Specialist officers that were promoted beyond general were promoted into the line ranks at the rank of Vice Admiral, although they usually retained the honorific branch titles of [[Air Marshal]], [[War commissar|War Commissar]], and Master Engineer, according to branch. The junior ranks of specialist officers, Captain and below, had their ranks prefixed by ''Flight'', ''Support'', or ''Engineering'' depending on the branch they served under. In the case of Flight Branch pilots, they also had their own positional titles: [[Squadron Leader/Legends|Squadron Leader]], [[Wing Commander/Legends|Wing Commander]], and [[Group Captain]]. TIE Squadron Leaders, normally Flight Captains, used the insignia of a ship's captain, as a fighter unit was considered the equivalent of a small-ship command. The [[Code cylinder/Legends|code cylinders]] worn by specialist officers served purely as insignia.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

In addition to plaques, the Imperials utilized code cylinders to signify their position in addition to their pragmatic use of regulating computer use aboard Imperial Navy ships, with the number used being dependent on the rank. Captains and Lieutenants generally had only one code cylinder, while Admirals, Commodores or Commanders had two, a Fleet Admiral had three and a High Admiral had four. Specialist ranking officers also utilized code cylinders, although their use was purely decorative as insignia.<ref name="The Essential Guide To Warfare" />

==Equipment==
After the creation of the New Order, and especially after the massive buildup orders issued after the Battle of Yavin, the Navy was issued top-of-the-line equipment throughout the upper ranks of the Imperial fleet. The equipment was standardized, which was largely a response to the Old Republic, which had developed so many equipment designs that most cadets served with units which possessed no equipment resembling that on which they had trained. Most old equipment in large quantities was in lower, system-level units.<ref name="ISB2" />

===Uniforms===
[[File:Imperial_Command_LBE.png|thumb|right|250px|An Imperial naval captain]]
{{Main|Imperial military uniforms/Legends}}
Personnel of the Imperial Navy wore a diverse assortment of uniforms according to their particular branch of service. Officers usually wore a [[Imperial officer's uniform/Legends|gray-green uniform]] with a double-breasted tunic, trousers, and a matching cap displaying an [[Officer's disk/Legends|officer's disc]], although officers who were veteran TIE pilots of the Starfighter Corps and/or security officers wore a black version of the uniform resembling the official uniform for officers of the Stormtrooper Corps instead. The Imperial Navy troopers wore all-black [[Jumpsuit/Legends|jumpsuits]], [[Utility belt/Legends|utility belts]], and swept-back black helmets for security duties and direct combat situations. Noncommissioned officers, including technicians and specialists, wore black or gray jumpsuits with a black cap, a forearm computer, and the [[Imperial crest/Legends|Imperial crest]] on the shoulder.<ref name="Handbook" />

Imperial gunners wore distinctive clamshell helmets and all-black duty uniforms with partial body armor. The TIE pilots wore environmentally sealed [[Flight suit/Legends|flight suits]] with a breastplate that housed a life-support unit. Hoses from the life-support unit piped oxygen into the pilots' sealed helmets.<ref name="Handbook" /> Both gunners and TIE pilots had the Imperial Navy crest adorning the front of their helmets (the gunners a single crest at the center, and the pilots two crests, one adorning each side of the front). Although the TIE/sa bomber pilots technically had a slightly different uniform that exposed part of their face due to the TIE/sa bomber possessing life-support capabilities, they in practice wore the same uniforms as other TIE pilots as a precaution in case of emergencies.<ref name="Complete Cross-Sections">''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]''</ref>

The most distinctive Naval uniforms were the all-white [[Grand Admiral's uniform/Legends|uniforms of the Grand Admirals]], who uniquely among Imperial personnel had the right to wear gold epaulets with their uniforms.<ref name="Handbook" />

Those with the rank of [[Commander Fleet Operations]] wore a specialized uniform during naval operations. It was composed of a black jumpsuit and gloves, as well as an all-encompassing helmet that had two ridges at the top and five pink lights on the front. Similar to the Imperial gunners, their helmet was adorned with the Imperial Navy crest at the front.<ref name="Base of Operations" />

===Droids===
A number of corporations produced [[Droid/Legends|droids]] for the near-exclusive use by the Imperial Navy. One of the most common was the [[MSE-6 series repair droid/Legends|MSE-6 "Mouse" Droid]] produced by [[Rebaxan Columni/Legends|Rebaxan Columni]]. After an attempt by the company to produce a droid pet proved to be a marketing disaster, the Imperial Navy, desperately short of droids in its early years, bought the entire production line.<ref name="Droids">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> The Navy used them as couriers for high-priority, high-security messages that could not be trusted to radio, and for simple maintenance like floor polishing and spot-welding.<ref name="Handbook" />

[[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]]' [[RA-7 protocol droid/Legends|RA-7 protocol droid]] was issued as an officer's adjutant, schedule-keeper, and translator, the last duty being necessary in the event that foreign emissaries were welcomed upon an officer's vessel.<ref name="Handbook" /> However, their real purpose was to secretly monitor officers for the [[Imperial Security Bureau/Legends|Imperial Security Bureau]] to ensure loyalty. Owing to the large number of high-ranking officers aboard the first Death Star, many RA-7s could be found there, to the point that they became known as the "Death Star Droid." The Death Star's destruction at the Battle of Yavin atomized most of the production line.<ref name="Droids" />

Arakyd's [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]] were used by the Navy for long-range reconnaissance. Deployed in [[Hyperdrive pod/Legends|hyperspace pods]], they operated autonomously when they reached their destination, relaying their findings back through secure Imperial wavelengths. They were equipped with a self-destruct sequence in the event that they were discovered, being activated when they were tagged by a blaster bolt.<ref name="Handbook" /> Death Squadron deployed thousands of Viper probe droids into the [[Western Reaches/Legends|Western Reaches]] in 3 ABY in search of the Rebellion's primary base of operations. One such probe droid eventually uncovered [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] of [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].<ref name="TEGTVAV" /><ref name="ESB" />

The Navy used [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton's]] [[R-series/Legends|R-series]] astromech droids for advanced maintenance. Painted in Naval black and gray, they operated in hangar bays to repair and maintain fighters and shuttles, or in engine rooms to calculate hyperspace coordinates and provide updated navigational data.<ref name="Handbook" />

==Ships==
The Imperial Navy used an overall strategy of focusing on capital ship firepower rather than starfighter superiority. This was reflected through the design of their starships, the formation of their naval units and the overall organization of the force. The most recognizable symbol of the Imperial Starfleet was the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]], which peaked at over twenty-five thousand vessels,<ref name="SOTP" /> although millions of starships of different designs were fielded for various purposes.

Super Star Destroyers became infamous for their size and armament, but some also contributed to the fleets as [[Mobile repair base|logistics vessels]]<ref name="SOTG07">[[Starships of the Galaxy (Saga Edition)|''Starships of the Galaxy'', Saga Edition]]</ref> and starfighter carriers. The Super Star Destroyer's intended role by Palpatine was to act as a command ship for Imperial forces in a specific sector, with there being one SSD per sector.<ref name="Handbook" />

Most major capital ships, battlestations and logistics vessels were constructed by Kuat Drive Yards, [[Loronar Corporation/Legends|Loronar Corporation]], and [[Rendili StarDrive/Legends|Rendili StarDrive]] during the height of the Galactic Empire.<ref name="TISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> The shipyards at [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] supplied the Empire with [[Gunship/Legends|gunships]], [[Corvette/Legends|corvettes]] and larger cruisers.<ref name="ANH" /> Additionally, countless shipyards supplied the Imperial Starfleet with support ships such as [[Carrack-class light cruiser/Legends|''Carrack''-class light cruisers]], [[Lancer-class frigate/Legends|''Lancer''-class frigates]], [[Strike-class medium cruiser|''Strike''-class cruisers]], and [[Ton-Falk-class escort carrier|''Ton-Falk''-class escort carriers]]. Interdictor cruisers, and to some extent [[Interdictor-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Interdictor-equipped]] Star Destroyers, also served a vital role in the Imperial fleet by blocking the enemy from exiting hyperspace. These acted as a means to patrol trade routes and enforce custom checkpoints, often doing random traffic inspections to discourage smuggling. Although the interdictors were made more important due to the Rebels' hit and hype tactics, [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] noted that their relative rarity compared to the more traditional warships was probably the only reason the Rebel Alliance survived the Empire, let alone defeated it.<ref name="Handbook" />

Several classified Imperial vessels possessed functional cloaking devices, powered by stygian [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] mined from the [[Dreighton Nebula/Legends|Dreighton Nebula]]. However, because the supply of crystals had nearly run dry by the time of the Galactic Civil War, with the consequential increase in expenses, these ships' use of cloaking devices diminished. In large part because of the diminished supply, research was conducted into alternate power materials for cloaking devices, with the Dreighton Nebula remaining under martial quarantine.
